analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches, changelog head and supplied inference BASE excerpts. The changes are documentation only in this batch. docs/architecture/inference.md head 3541–3575 describes setup/control listeners following cable addresses and pairing identity every five seconds, stopping on absent pairing, retaining listeners on unreadable storage, and dropping control state when either member changes. changelog.d/cluster-service-follows-repair.md:3–6 states the same lifecycle and restart limitation. These affect peer authentication, stale authority and availability, relevant to A-001, A-003, TB-003, TB-007 and the endpoint-lifecycle concerns of T-053, but do not establish a coordinator authorization change or a concrete regression. Pairing identity explicitly excludes the edge secret; the documented fresh link epoch is therefore a security-relevant contract to verify, not evidence of a bypass.
The surrounding BASE excerpts describe admission, authenticated tenant cache scopes, native retirement and memory accounting. They are unchanged here; differences from historical T-041 prose are not attributable to this PR. No changed plaintext exposure, billing, attestation or cache control is supported by these units.
Integration must examine ClusterService.swift (listenerChange/ensureResponder), ClusterServiceControl.swift (ensureControlResponder/ensureControl), and ClusterSetupLinkExchange.swift (Pairing.Identity/Responder): verify fresh epoch generation, authenticated peer pins, old connection/task retirement during listener replacement, and that unreadable storage cannot silently accept a newly revoked pairing. Confirm control-state invalidation covers both local and peer key changes without granting serving permission. Those implementations are not supplied in this batch, so the documented lifecycle remains unverified rather than safe or vulnerable.
